title: Strong and trustworthy
hook: the best to hire is the strong and the trustworthy (28:26)
carry: the kind of job nobody will check

segments.voice: Yesterday, haya', and your line was modesty is a walk. Which room did you walk into slowly, and what did you say plainly? Day five hundred twenty-six.

Every hiring manager has a list. Experience, references, a good interview, a degree from the right place. Musa has none of it. He's a fugitive with no money, no letters, no home, sitting in a stranger's house in Madyan. He has told the old man his whole story, and the old man has said, don't be afraid, you've escaped from the wrongdoing people. Then one of the daughters speaks up and gives him a reference. Her case rests on two words, and she has seen him earn both.

She says to her father, hire him. Pickthall: "the best (man) that thou canst hire is the strong, the trustworthy." In Arabic, al-qawiyy al-amin. Qawiyy is strong, able, capable of the work. Amin is trustworthy, from the same root as amana, a trust, and iman, faith. How does she know? She's seen both with her own eyes. Strength at the well, where he watered a whole flock that had been waiting behind the shepherds. And trustworthiness on the way home. Commentators tell, from a report attributed to 'Umar, that Musa asked her to walk behind him and call out the way, so that he wouldn't be looking at her as she walked. That detail is from commentary, not the verse. But the point stands either way: she'd watched him work, and she'd watched him behave when no one else was looking. Here's why both words matter. Strength without trust is a danger: a capable person you can't rely on. Trust without strength is a disappointment: a good person who can't do the job. The same pair turns up once more, in Surah An-Naml, from an unlikely mouth: a jinn offering to fetch the Queen of Sheba's throne says he is strong and trustworthy for the job. The old man takes his daughter's advice. He offers Musa marriage to one of his daughters, for eight years of work, or ten if he chooses. And Musa answers, whichever term I complete, let there be no injustice to me. A contract made between two people who each had reason to trust the other. A hadith in Bukhari warns that when trust is lost, the Hour is near.
screen: `AL-QAWIYY AL-AMIN.` · `STRENGTH SEEN AT THE WELL.` · `TRUST SEEN ON THE WALK HOME.` · `BOTH, OR NEITHER IS ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: be both at work. Sit, and let the breath settle. Think of the work in front of you today, paid or unpaid: a job, a class, a household, caring for someone. Ask two questions honestly. Where am I strong but not quite trustworthy? A corner I cut, a promise I let slide. And where am I trustworthy but not strong? Something I mean well about but haven't learned to do properly. Pick one of the two to work on today. If you pray, you can ask for strength and trust together. The bell holds the time.
Al-amin. The daughter's word for Musa: trustworthy, safe to trust with the work. Today's word.
Your line: the kind of job nobody will check. Today, finish one task completely and well. Day five hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Muslims often cite 28:26 when speaking of hiring, leadership and work ethic, holding that a person given a role should be both capable and trustworthy.

thank him and send him on.

original.note: Arabic: the strong, the trustworthy; the daughter's words for Musa in 28:26.

trapdoor: what you thought: a nice compliment.
what it means: a two-part test for anyone given a job: able to do it, and safe to trust with it.
what a scholar hears: al-qawiyy al-amin, the same pair a jinn claims for himself in 27:39; amin from a-m-n, the root of amana and iman; and the hadith that lost trust signals the Hour (Bukhari 59).

sources.quoted: the best (man) that thou canst hire is the strong, the trustworthy.

sources.ref: Qur'an 28:25–28 (the old man, the offer, the contract)
Qur'an 27:39 (the jinn: strong and trustworthy for the task)

notes: Pickthall 28:26 quoted from memory; confirm wording.
The 'walk behind me' detail is reported in tafsir (e.g. Ibn Kathir, via a report from 'Umar); labeled as commentary. Confirm.
The old man of Madyan is not named in the Qur'an; many identify him with Shu'ayb, others disagree. The script leaves him unnamed.

Audit: the teach claimed Surah Yusuf (12:55) pairs 'strong' and 'trustworthy', but Yusuf's words there are 'careful guardian, knowing'; replaced with 27:39, where qawiyy and amin actually recur, and updated the trapdoor and sources. Also cut the unsourced 'shortest job recommendation in scripture' line from the hook.
